steps.title: Verify System Hardware and Laser Status
steps.instruction: Ensure the laser and PMT are operational and correctly configured.

substeps.instruction: Confirm the Laser is on and not shuttered.
Confirm the LCDR on the laser path is not shuttered and no beam-blocks are present.
Confirm the PMT is on and the set voltage is between 600 and 650 volts.

steps.title: Position and Focus Tissue
steps.instruction: Align the tissue beneath the objective and establish a focal plane.

substeps.instruction: Cut sections by clicking the 'Slice' button in Orchestrator until a part of the tissue (e.g., brain stem) is exposed.

Position tissue directly beneath the objective via visual inspection or by moving the stage (Left, Right, Backward, Forward) in Orchestrator while maximizing IR reflection brightness using the Newport IRV1-1700 Infrared viewer.
Set the Piezo control to 200.
Move the Z-stage Up/Down in 50 micron steps in Orchestrator, capturing a 2D image at each step until the tissue is visible.
If the image is lost after clicking 'Slice', adjust the Piezo control (range 0 to 400).

steps.title: Resolve Sine Wave Noise
steps.instruction: Clear cross-hatched patterns or tissue distortion caused by motion controller issues.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the tissue surface in the bath is not too close to the objective; if necessary, drop the stage by 1000 micrometers or remove the bath.
Close all programs on master and slave computers, including Orchestrator, Vivace, and PMT control.
Turn off the power switch on the back of the black Motion Control box.
Disconnect power connectors from the X and Y stage controllers (Mercury C-863 DC Motor Controllers) on the controller board.
Wait 10 seconds, then reconnect power to the X and Y stage controllers.
Turn on the power to the Motion Control box.
Click 'Connect all' from the Services tab in Orchestrator (do not click 'Reference Stage' yet).
Type 'MN' (Motor oN) in the CMD command boxes for X and Y stages and click Send.

Verify X and Y controllers have green lights and no red lights. If the top LED is red, reinitialize via Orchestrator. If both top and bottom LEDs are red, disconnect power for 10 seconds, reconnect, and then reinitialize via Orchestrator.
Initialize the stage by clicking 'Reference Stage' in the Services tab.
Click 'Slice' in the Protocol tab to mimic sectioning.
Capture a 2D image in the Imaging tab to verify the noise is cleared.

steps.title: Resolve Moiré Pattern Noise
steps.instruction: Fix quasi-periodic bright horizontal patches caused by laser pulse instability.

substeps.instruction: Restart the computers in the following sequence: shut down the Slave, restart the Master, then restart the Slave.

steps.title: Adjust Vibratome Blade Angle
steps.instruction: Correct the cutting blade angle if the imaging plane is consistently above or below the tissue.

substeps.instruction: Remove the vibratome arm from the system and secure it to the alignment tool.
Use the adjustment screw to set the desired angle of attack.
Adjust set screws on the vibratome arm until the razor blade is horizontal and level (optionally use a dial indicator to observe displacements).

steps.title: Adjust Objective Assembly Height
steps.instruction: Modify the height of the objective assembly if the tissue surface falls below the piezo range (below focal plane when piezo is at 400 microns).

substeps.instruction: Support the assembly from the bottom and loosen the two screws (S) using 2.5mm hex drivers.
Drop the assembly by approximately 1mm and tighten the screws (S).
Fine-tune the height using the fine-pitch adjustment screw (H) (pitch is 4/mm; one turn right raises by 0.25mm/250 microns, one turn left drops by 0.25mm/250 microns).
Ensure the fine-pitch adjustment screw is in contact with the reference point.

steps.title: Troubleshoot Low Signal Intensity
steps.instruction: Address low signal caused by bubbles, alignment, or laser operation.

substeps.instruction: Check for and remove air bubbles from the front element of the objective or the bath using a small transfer pipet.
Verify laser operation and alignment; increase laser power via the quarter-wave plate if necessary.

steps.title: Resolve Scanning Control Issues
steps.instruction: Troubleshoot failures in the scanning mirrors or control box.

substeps.instruction: Verify cables are properly connected to the scanning control box and scanning mirrors.
If unresolved, power off the scanning control box for 10 seconds and power it back on.
If still unresolved, reboot the PC.
Capture a screen JPEG of the error if possible.
Record all relevant information: system history, state at time of crash, and hardware state.
Attempt a simple reboot to clear the error.
If the error persists or affects data quality, contact Tissue Vision with the screen capture and recorded information.

steps.title: Establish Remote Support Session
steps.instruction: Connect with Tissue Vision support via WebEx.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the target computer is connected to the internet.
Obtain a WebEx session ID and login path from Tissue Vision.
Connect to the session using Firefox or IE.
Grant desktop control to the remote party when prompted.
